reports.title: Basic medical history – Initial diagnosis Multiple Myeloma

sections.name: Medical history
sections.content: The 53-year-old female patient presents for further evaluation of an incidental finding. In the context of a routine blood draw by the primary care physician (01/2024), a pronounced hyperglobulinemia with elevated total protein (106 g/l) and a normochromic anemia (Hb 9,2 g/dl) were detected. The patient reports fatigue and reduced performance for approximately 3 months. Denies bone pain. No renal symptoms. No B symptoms.

sections.name: Pre-existing conditions
sections.content: No hematologic diseases. Hypothyroidism treated with L-Thyroxin. No hypertension, no diabetes mellitus. No known kidney disease.

sections.name: Family history
sections.content: No hematologic malignancies known in the family. Mother diagnosed with breast cancer (age at diagnosis 68 years).

reports.title: Bone marrow biopsy – Initial diagnosis

sections.name: Question
sections.content:
Suspected multiple myeloma. Bone marrow aspiration and core biopsy dated 10.02.2024.
Macroscopy: A representative core cylinder, approx. 1,8 cm in length.  
Processing: HE, Giemsa, PAS, Gomori, CD138, MUM1, kappa, lambda.

sections.name: Findings
sections.content:
Normocellular to mildly hypercellular bone marrow core cylinder (cellularity approx. 50–60%) with moderately extensive interstitial and focal infiltrate of mature plasma cells.
Infiltration grade: approx. 35% of nucleated cells.  
Immunohistochemistry: CD138+, MUM1+, IgG+, lambda light chains dominant, kappa negative.

sections.name: FISH result
sections.content:
FISH analysis (02/2024, plasma cell gating):
- del(17p): negative  
- t(4;14): negative  
- t(14;16): negative  
- 1q21 gain: negative  
Conclusion: No high‑risk cytogenetics detected. Standard risk.

sections.name: Diagnosis
sections.content:
Multiple myeloma, IgG lambda light chain.
ISS stage I (β2‑microglobulin 2,1 mg/l, albumin 4,2 g/dl).  
R‑ISS stage I (ISS I, no high‑risk cytogenetics, LDH normal).

reports.title: Whole‑body MRI – Staging

sections.name: Findings
sections.content:
Whole‑body MRI (1,5 Tesla, STIR and T1w) dated 15.02.2024.
Bone marrow: Focal heterogeneous signal pattern with isolated small STIR‑positive foci in the sacroiliac region (max. 6 mm). No diffuse involvement pattern.  
Spine: No osteolysis. No pathological fracture. Normal bone marrow signal.  
Extramedullary manifestation: Not detected.  
Conclusion: Isolated small foci compatible with focal myelomatous involvement, no extensive bone disease.

reports.title: Flow cytometry – Bone marrow initial diagnosis

sections.name: Result
sections.content: Multiparameter flow cytometry (bone marrow aspirate from 10.02.2024). Detection of a clonal plasma cell population: 32% of nucleated cells. Phenotype: CD138+, CD38+, CD19-, CD56+, CD45-, lambda+, kappa-. BCMA expression: positive (MFI 1840). No detection of minimal residual disease (MRD) by NGF at this time not meaningful (first diagnosis, no therapy).

reports.title: Physician letter – Initial diagnosis and treatment planning

sections.name: Diagnoses
sections.content:
Hematologic diagnoses: Multiple myeloma, IgG light chain lambda (first diagnosis 02/2024) ISS stage I, R‑ISS stage I Standard‑risk cytogenetics (FISH without high‑risk abnormality) Osseous manifestation: isolated small foci (MRI), no overt osteolysis CRAB criteria: anemia (Hb 9,2 g/dl), otherwise no organ dysfunction

Secondary diagnoses: hypothyroidism, L‑thyroxine 100 µg/d No cardiac comorbidities

sections.name: History and examination
sections.content: The 53‑year‑old patient is in good general condition. Past history: fatigue, no bone pain, no renal symptoms. ECOG performance status: 0. Clinical examination: no lymphadenopathy, no hepatosplenomegaly.

sections.name: Prior therapy
sections.content: No prior therapy.

sections.name: Treatment plan
sections.content:
Because of age (53 years) and ECOG 0, the patient is transplant‑eligible. Initiate first‑line therapy with VRd (bortezomib/lenalidomide/dexamethasone) starting 01.03.2024. Bortezomib 1,3 mg/m² s.c. on days 1, 4, 8, 11 of a 21‑day cycle. Lenalidomide 25 mg/d orally on days 1–14. Dexamethasone 40 mg orally on days 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 9, 11, 12. Zoledronic acid 4 mg i.v. every 4 weeks.

After 3–4 cycles remission assessment. With adequate response (≥PR): stem‑cell mobilization and high‑dose melphalan + autologous SCT planned.

sections.name: Transfusion
sections.content: Due to symptomatic anemia (Hb 9,2 g/dl, exertional dyspnea) transfusion of 2 erythrocyte concentrates on 19.02.2024. Post‑transfusion Hb 11,4 g/dl.

sections.name: Procedure
sections.content: Visit after cycle 1 (approx. 22.03.2024) for tolerability and laboratory assessment. Platelet/coagulation monitoring weekly during the first 4 weeks.

reports.title: Tumor board decision – Initial diagnosis MM, treatment planning

sections.name: Reason for discussion
sections.content: Initial diagnosis of multiple myeloma, IgG light chain lambda, in a 53‑year‑old transplant‑eligible patient.

sections.name: Findings
sections.content: MM IgG lambda, ISS I, R‑ISS I, standard‑risk cytogenetics. Anemia (Hb 9,2 g/dl) as the only CRAB criterion. No renal insufficiency, no hypercalcemia, no overt osteolysis.

sections.name: Resolution
sections.content: Consensus: VRd induction therapy, goal ≥VGPR after 4 cycles. Response ≥PR: stem‑cell mobilization and HD‑Melphalan + autologous SZT. Inclusion in GMMG‑HD10 / DSMM XX study evaluated: patient essentially meets inclusion criteria (newly diagnosed MM, transplant‑eligible, ECOG 0–1, age <70 years). Counseling and informed consent will be offered.

sections.content:

Labor 22.03.2024: IgG 38,4 g/l (baseline 52,3 g/l, –27%), Hb 12,8 g/dl, Leukozyten 6,2 G/l, Neutrophile 3,8 G/l.  
Adverse events: tingling of fingertips (neuropathy grade 1), fatigue grade 1, no neutropenia grade 3/4.

reports.title: Physician letter – VRd cycle 2 follow‑up

sections.name: Diagnoses
sections.content:
Multiple myeloma, IgG LK lambda (ED 02/2024)
After 2 cycles VRd: early response

sections.name: Current course
sections.content:
VRd cycle 2 (22.03.–11.04.2024) completed without complications. Labor 19.04.2024: IgG 26,1 g/l (‑50% compared with baseline 52,3 g/l), FLK lambda 142 mg/l (‑54%). Immunofixation remains positive. Hb 13,0 g/dl, Leukozyten 5,8 G/l, Neutrophile 3,4 G/l.
Response after 2 cycles: PR (reduction of M‑protein >50%).  
Neuropathy grade 1 persists (tingling of fingertips, feet), no dose reduction required.

sections.name: Maintenance medication
sections.content: As before. Rivaroxaban 10 mg continued.

sections.name: Further procedure
sections.content: Start VRd cycle 3 on 12.04.2024. After cycle 4 remission assessment and decision regarding stem‑cell mobilization. ECOG: 0

reports.title: Tumor board decision – Interim review after 2 cycles of VRd

sections.name: Reason for discussion
sections.content: Follow‑up assessment in newly diagnosed MM IgG lambda, ISS I, after 2 cycles of VRd induction.

sections.name: Findings
sections.content: IgG 26.1 g/L (baseline 52.3 g/L), free light chain lambda 142 mg/L. Response: PR after 2 cycles. Tolerability good. Neuropathy grade 1.

sections.name: Decision
sections.content: Continue VRd cycles 3 and 4. Remission assessment after cycle 4. If ≥VGPR: stem‑cell mobilization after cycle 6, then high‑dose melphalan + ASCT. If <PR after cycle 4: discuss therapy adjustment. No change to the current therapy.

reports.title: Physician letter – VRd cycle 3 follow‑up

sections.name: Diagnoses
sections.content:
Multiple myeloma, IgG lambda (diagnosed 02/2024)
After 3 cycles of VRd: PR (progressive response)

sections.name: Current course
sections.content:
Cycle 3 (12 Apr–02 May 2024) completed without issues. Laboratory 17 May 2024: IgG 16.2 g/L (‑69 %), free light chain lambda 64 mg/L (‑79 %), kappa/lambda 0.23 (still clonal). Hb 13.4 g/dL, neutrophils 3.2 G/L. No grade 3/4 neutropenia.
Assessment: Persistent deep PR, trend toward VGPR. Immunofixation positive.

sections.name: Chronic medication
sections.content: As before. Zoledronic acid administration 3.

sections.name: Further procedure
sections.content: Cycle 4 started 03 May 2024. Remission assessment planned after cycle 4 (≈ 10 Jun 2024).

reports.title: Physician letter – Remission assessment after 4 cycles of VRd

sections.name: Diagnoses
sections.content:
Multiple myeloma, IgG lambda (diagnosed 02/2024)
After 4 cycles of VRd: VGPR  
Current: bortezomib + lenalidomide + dexamethasone (ongoing)

sections.name: Therapeutic response
sections.content:
After 4 cycles VRd:
- IgG: 9,8 g/l (baseline 52 g/l)
- Immunofixation in serum: positive (weak, M‑protein detectable)
- Free light chains lambda: 28 mg/l (baseline 310 mg/l)
- Kappa/Lambda ratio: 0,4 (slightly decreased, still clonal)
Assessment: VGPR (very good partial response)

VRd tolerability: Peripheral neuropathy grade 1 (tingling in hands, no functional impairment). Fatigue grade 1. No grade 3/4 neutropenia. No infection. No pneumonia.

Subsequently: high‑dose melphalan + autologous SCT.
No CD38 antibody, no BiTE, no CAR‑T therapy received to date.
Patient exposed to IMiD (lenalidomide) and PI (bortezomib), but never received a CD38 antibody.

reports.title: Physician letter – VRd cycle 5 follow‑up

sections.name: Diagnoses
sections.content:
Multiple myeloma, IgG light chain lambda (diagnosed 02/2024)
After 5 cycles VRd: VGPR (confirmed)

sections.name: Current course
sections.content:
Cycle 5 (05.06.–25.06.2024) completed. Laboratory 21.06.2024: IgG 8,4 g/l, free light chain lambda 18,2 mg/l (now within normal range), free light chain kappa 10,8 mg/l, kappa/lambda 0,59 (normal). Immunofixation: positive (weak, M‑protein still detectable). Hb 13,6 g/dl. Neutrophils 3,0 G/l.
Assessment: VGPR confirmed – marked reduction of M‑protein >90 % versus baseline.
Neuropathy grade 1 stable, no progression.

reports.title: Tumor board decision – VGPR after 5 VRd, stem‑cell mobilization planned

sections.name: Reason for meeting
sections.content: Planning stem‑cell mobilization and autologous transplantation after VGPR under VRd induction.

sections.name: Findings
sections.content: VGPR after 5 cycles VRd. IgG 8,4 g/l, immunofixation positive. Free light chain lambda normalized. ECOG 0. No relevant comorbidity. Transplant eligibility confirmed.

sections.name: Decision
sections.content: Complete cycle 6 VRd, then stem cell mobilization with G‑CSF (10 µg/kg/d) starting day 4 after cycle end. Use of plerixafor reserved for insufficient mobilization. Goal: ≥4 × 10^6 CD34+/kg (2 transplants). High‑dose melphalan 200 mg/m² + autologous SCT planned for 08/2024. Afterwards: lenalidomide maintenance therapy.

reports.title: Whole‑body PET‑CT – staging before SCT

sections.name: Full report
sections.content:
Clinical information: MM IgG lambda, VGPR after 6 cycles VRd, staging before planned autologous stem cell transplantation.

Question: Detection of active myelomatous lesions? Comparison with prior examination (whole‑body MRI 02/2024).  

Prior imaging: whole‑body MRI 15.02.2024.  

Findings: No FDG‑avid lesions detected osseously or extramedullary. No pathologically increased metabolism in bone marrow (no SUV‑max elevation above liver median). The previously known small STIR‑positive foci in the iliosacral region from the MRI prior study show correspondingly no increased FDG signal. No new osteolyses detected. No lymphadenopathy. Normal lungs, liver, spleen.  

Impression: Complete metabolic remission (CMR, Deauville 1). No active myelomatous lesions detectable. Findings consistent with VGPR/CR on metabolic level. Suitable for stem cell transplantation.

reports.title: Physician letter – VRd cycle 6 completed, mobilization planning

sections.name: Diagnoses
sections.content: Multiple myeloma, IgG LC lambda (diagnosed 02/2024) After 6 cycles VRd: VGPR (PET‑CT: CMR) Planning stem cell mobilization from 22.07.2024

sections.name: Current course
sections.content: Cycle 6 VRd (26.06.–16.07.2024) completed. Laboratory 19.07.2024: IgG 7.6 g/L, immunofixation positive (weak). Free light chain lambda 14.8 mg/L (normal range), κ/λ 0.71. PET‑CT 15.07.2024: complete metabolic remission (CMR, Deauville 1). Patient is transplant‑eligible.

sections.name: Current medication
sections.content: G‑CSF (filgrastim) 10 µg/kg/d subcutaneously from 22.07.2024 (day 1 mobilization). All other medications as before, lenalidomide paused from 17.07.2024.

sections.name: Further procedure
sections.content: Stem cell mobilization: G‑CSF days 1–5. CD34+ count in peripheral blood from day 4. Apheresis planned when CD34+ ≥10/µL (approximately 25–26.07.2024). Goal: ≥4 × 10^6 CD34+/kg. Inpatient admission for ASCT: 12.08.2024.

reports.title: Physician letter – stem cell mobilization and apheresis

sections.name: Diagnoses
sections.content: Multiple myeloma, IgG LC lambda (diagnosed 02/2024) Stem cell mobilization successfully completed

sections.name: Current course
sections.content: G‑CSF mobilization (filgrastim 10 µg/kg/d subcutaneously) from 22.07.2024. CD34+ count peripheral blood day 4 (25.07.2024): 42/µL – sufficient for apheresis. Apheresis 25.07.2024 and 26.07.2024 (2 sessions of 3 h each via central venous access). Collected CD34+ cells: 6.2 × 10^6/kg (sufficient for 2 transplants). Cryopreservation performed. Tolerability: grade 2 bone pain under G‑CSF (ibuprofen as needed). No fever, no infection, no plerixafor required.

sections.name: Further procedure
sections.content: Inpatient admission for high‑dose melphalan + ASCT on 12.08.2024. Patient is informed and pre‑operative examinations (ECG, echocardiogram, laboratory) will be performed on 08.08.2024 on an outpatient basis.

reports.title: Medical report – Inpatient admission for ASCT / high-dose melphalan conditioning

sections.name: Diagnoses
sections.content: Multiple myeloma, IgG light chain lambda (diagnosed 02/2024) After 6 cycles of VRd: VGPR, CMR on PET‑CT Admission for autologous stem cell transplantation

sections.name: Admission
sections.content: Inpatient admission on 12.08.2024 for high-dose melphalan conditioning and autologous stem cell transplantation. Admission laboratory 12.08.2024: Hb 13.1 g/dl, leukocytes 5.4 G/l, neutrophils 3.2 G/l, platelets 210 G/l. Creatinine 0.85 mg/dl, eGFR 86 ml/min. IgG 7.6 g/l. LDH 202 U/l. ECG: sinus rhythm. Echocardiography: EF 65%, no left ventricular dysfunction, no effusion. Conditioning: high-dose melphalan 200 mg/m² IV over 30 min on 12.08.2024 (D‑2). BSA = 1.72 m², total dose 344 mg. Adequate hyperhydration (3 l/m²/day IV) and antiemesis (ondansetron + aprepitant).

sections.name: Stem cell return
sections.content: Reinfusion of cryopreserved autologous stem cells (6.2 × 10⁶ CD34⁺/kg) on 14.08.2024 (D0). Infusion without complications.

sections.name: Further procedure
sections.content: G‑CSF (filgrastim) starting D+5 (19.08.2024). Daily blood count and vital sign monitoring. Isolation until engraftment.

reports.title: Medical report – ASCT discharge after engraftment

sections.name: Diagnoses

sections.content: Engraftment: neutrophils >0.5 G/l on day +8 (22.08.2024), platelets >20 G/l on day +7. Course uncomplicated. Mucositis: grade 1 (mild mucosal irritation, pain control with metamizole sufficient). No fever, no documented bacteremia. No transfusion‑requiring anemia (Hb nadir 8.4 g/dl on day +7, no red cell transfusion required). Discharge laboratory 26.08.2024: Hb 10.2 g/dl, leukocytes 4.8 G/l, neutrophils 2.9 G/l, platelets 86 G/l (rising). Creatinine 0.88 mg/dl.

reports.title: Whole‑body MRI – follow‑up post‑ASCT

sections.name: Full report
sections.content:
Clinical information: MM IgG lambda, after HD‑Melphalan + ASCT 08/2024, follow‑up.

Question: Residual myelomatous foci? Comparison with PET‑CT 07/2024 and baseline MRI 02/2024.  

Prior imaging: Whole‑body MRI 15.02.2024, PET‑CT 15.07.2024.  

Findings: Bone marrow: Largely homogeneous, fatty signal. No evidence of active STIR‑positive foci any more. Previously known small iliac‑sacral foci from the prior MRI no longer discernible. No new osseous lesions. No extramedullary pathology. Spine: No fractures, no new osteolyses.  

Assessment: Complete imaging‑morphologic remission. No evidence of residual myelomatous foci. Marked regression compared with prior study. Consistent with stringent complete response (sCR) on imaging level.

reports.title: Flow cytometry – MRD assessment post‑ASCT (NGF)

sections.name: Result
sections.content: Multiparameter flow cytometry of the bone‑marrow aspirate from 07.10.2024 (Next‑Generation Flow, EuroFlow panel, sensitivity 10^-5). Result: MRD‑NEGATIVE. No detection of a clonal plasma‑cell population with the aberrant phenotype CD138+/CD38+/CD19-/CD56+/lambda+. Proportion of aberrant plasma cells: <0,001% of nucleated cells (below the detection limit). Normal polyclonal plasma‑cell population: 0,08%. Conclusion: MRD negativity after ASCT confirmed (sensitivity threshold 10^-5).

reports.title: Bone marrow biopsy – Remission assessment post‑ASCT

sections.name: Findings
sections.content:
Bone marrow core biopsy from 07.10.2024.
Cellularity: approx. 40 % (age‑appropriate post‑ASCT).  
No evidence of a plasma cell infiltrate. Scattered plasma cells (normal, <1 % of nucleated cells). No clonality detectable.  
Immunohistochemistry: CD138 positive in isolated cells (normal plasma cells), kappa and lambda positivity evenly distributed (polyclonal).

sections.name: Diagnosis
sections.content: No evidence of a myeloma relapse. Histologically complete remission. Together with negative serum immunofixation and MRD negativity by NGF, the patient meets the criteria for a stringent complete remission (sCR).

sections.name: Remission assessment
sections.content:
Remission assessment after ASCT (Day +68):
- Serum IgG: 5.0 g/l (reference range)  
- Serum immunofixation: NEGATIVE (no M‑protein detectable)  
- Urine immunofixation: NEGATIVE  
- Free light chain lambda: 11.4 mg/l (reference range)  
- Free light chain kappa: 10.2 mg/l, Kappa/Lambda: 0.90 (reference range)  
- BM histology 07.10.2024: No plasma cell infiltrate, histologically CR  
- MRD by NGF (EuroFlow): Negative (<10⁻⁵)  
- PET‑CT/MRT 09/2024: Complete imaging‑morphological remission  

Overall assessment: Stringent complete remission (sCR), MRD‑negative. Best response since diagnosis.

reports.title: Tumor board decision – Lenalidomide maintenance therapy after ASCT

sections.name: Reason for discussion
sections.content: Planning maintenance therapy for sCR/MRD‑negative MM after ASCT in a 54‑year‑old patient.

sections.name: Findings
sections.content: sCR after VRd × 6 + HD‑Melphalan + ASCT. MRD‑negative by NGF. Standard‑risk cytogenetics.

sections.name: Decision
sections.content:
Start of lenalidomide maintenance therapy from 04.11.2024.
Dosage: Lenalidomide 10 mg/d p.o. days 1–21 of a 28‑day cycle (standard maintenance dose; consider 15 mg if no toxicity after 3 months).  
Planned duration: at least 2 years (until progression or unacceptable toxicity).  
MRD assessment every 6 months by NGF and immunofixation. Skeletal imaging if clinical suspicion.  
Thrombosis prophylaxis: Aspirin 100 mg/d together with lenalidomide.
